props.title: My Summer of Love
props.initialSlug: Two teen girls' intense bond leads to dark obsession

sections.content: My Summer of Love (2004) marks a breakthrough in British coming-of-age cinema, with director Pawel Pawlikowski crafting an intoxicating exploration of class, sexuality, and deception. The film launched Emily Blunt's career alongside Natalie Press, their electric chemistry echoing the raw intimacy of Peter Jackson's Heavenly Creatures (1994). Like Fish Tank (2009), it captures the volatile mix of teenage desire and class tension in working-class Britain, but with a dreamy, sun-drenched aesthetic that belies its darker themes.

sections.content: The film's portrayal of summer romance shares DNA with French New Wave classics like À nos amours (1983), where youth, sexuality, and identity intertwine in sun-bleached scenes. Pawlikowski's approach to class dynamics recalls An Education (2009), though he trades that film's period setting for contemporary Yorkshire's stark social divides. The religious elements, centered on Press's born-again Christian brother, add another layer of tension that echoes Breaking the Waves (1996)'s exploration of faith and desire.

What sets My Summer of Love apart is its refusal to moralize or sensationalize its sapphic romance. Unlike earlier lesbian films like Desert Hearts (1985), it treats its characters' sexuality as matter-of-fact, focusing instead on the power dynamics of class and belief. The film's dreamy cinematography by Ryszard Lenczewski creates a heightened reality that recalls The Virgin Suicides (1999), where teenage desire transforms mundane surroundings into something magical and dangerous. sections.content: While My Summer of Love emerges from Britain's social realist tradition, it shares more DNA with the sensual storytelling of Picnic at Hanging Rock (1975) than the kitchen sink drama of Rita, Sue and Bob Too (1987). Pawlikowski's approach influenced later British films like God's Own Country (2017) and Lady Macbeth (2016), which similarly blend class consciousness with raw emotional intensity and richly textured visuals.
